original_value:
New technologies are rapidly changing mobile learning and making it difficult to control. In addition to educational factors and learning content, a modern mobile learning system must take into account the technical and personal aspects of learning, the devices and aspects related to its evolution and interoperability. Teaching on the other hand has also evolved involving more flexibility in tasks and learning stages, thus using modern technologies that offer more alternatives now. In addition, such tasks may be specific to the learning content as well as the learning context or furthermore the learner's environment.

Traditionally, mobile platform design relies on the skills of a mobile developer whose knowledge allows him to design mobile applications that are useful to users. But with mobile learning, the design phase involves more than just mobile development skills. For example, if you are designing a platform for practical work, the instructors responsible for the training should be involved. However, the empirical results show that educators do not integrate technology effectively into their curricula. To enable these instructors to develop mobile learning platforms, it is important to facilitate their integration through a theoretical model that will take into account all the ingredients necessary to complete this learning and to balance them in order to ensure its efficiency. In this study authors used a thematic synthesis methodology to present a framework for mobile devices integration in learning. They focused on three models that they think are the most cited in the field of ICT (information and communication technologies) integration in learning.

The five-axis framework consists of enriching the TPACK framework(Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge model in order to more precisely address mobile learning by covering the following parts: pedagogy, content, mobile technology, learning environment and learner’s profile. It describes relatively in depth the various factors involved as well as the effective interconnection to be ensured to achieve an optimal and efficient integration of m-learning. Balancing those five parts will be a matter of plural reflection when designing or consulting on a mobile learning platform.

result.paraphrase:
New technologies are rapidly transforming mobile learning, making it harder to manage. Besides educational factors and learning content, a contemporary mobile learning system has to consider the technical and personal dimensions of learning, along with the devices and issues tied to their evolution and interoperability. Teaching has likewise changed, with greater flexibility in tasks and learning stages, and it now makes use of modern technologies that provide more options. These tasks may also be tied to the learning content, the learning context, or the learner’s environment.

Traditionally, mobile platform design depends on the expertise of a mobile developer whose knowledge enables the creation of mobile applications useful to users. With mobile learning, however, the design stage requires more than mobile development skills alone. For instance, when designing a platform for practical work, the instructors in charge of the training need to be involved. Yet empirical findings show that educators do not effectively integrate technology into their curricula. To help these instructors develop mobile learning platforms, their integration should be supported by a theoretical model that includes all the elements needed to complete this learning and balances them to ensure efficiency. In this study, the authors used thematic synthesis to propose a framework for integrating mobile devices into learning. They concentrated on three models that they regard as the most frequently cited in ICT integration in learning.

The five-axis framework extends the TPACK framework, the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge model, to address mobile learning more precisely by covering pedagogy, content, mobile technology, the learning environment, and the learner’s profile. It provides a fairly detailed description of the different factors involved, as well as the effective links that must be maintained to achieve optimal and efficient m-learning integration. Balancing these five elements requires multiple perspectives when designing or advising on a mobile learning platform.
